hints.content:
The function $h$ is negative $($i.e. $h(x)<0)$ whenever its graph is below the $x$-axis.

This is because the negative $y$-values are below the $x$-axis, and $y=h(x)$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by four. The graph of the function y equals h of x is above the x-axis from x equals negative five to x equals negative two. It is below the x-axis from x equals negative two to x equals three. It is above the x-axis after x equals three. The function decreases from x equals negative five to x equals one-half. It increases after x equals one-half  All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative two to x equals three.

hints.content: Out of our options, the only correct interval is $-1<x<1$.
